universal_proof: The integer-valued invariant B_p(L)=binom(lk(L_1,L_2),p) is a rational degree-p polynomial in a type-one integer linking invariant, hence type at most p over Q. Every singular alternating sum is an integer, so the rational zero for p+1 singular points is zero integrally; reduction modulo p preserves finite type. On coherent sigma^(2n) closures it is binom(n,p) mod p. In the Hopf generator replacing one crossing by odd x=2n-1 gives these links. n=0 and n=p give the same x modulo p but respective values0 and1. Any polynomial over F_p in x would give equal values. Negative lk values use integer generalized binomial coefficients, so B_p is an oriented labeled classical-link invariant on the whole domain; no unordered/unoriented claim.
